props.title: Ripples

cues.label: normal map: an image of which way each pixel faces

props.caption: ripple_strength 0 to 1.5 on one still normal map

B25.capture_spec: C17: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04a-normal-map, ripple_strength swept 0 to 1.5 across the beat (one static normal map: a NoiseTexture2D, As Normal Map, Seamless).
B25.visual_intent: Act title 'Ripples'; code card (the 04a fragment, NORMAL_MAP lit); the real cove: first one big flat sun glare, then as the strength rises the glare breaks into thousands of small glints.
B25.motion_claim: One big glare breaks into glints as the strength rises.
B25.runner_up: manim: light on a flat and a bumpy line
B25.why: The real glare breaking up is the claim; the drawing would only model it.

B26.visual_intent: Left: the real normal map (captures/normal_a.png, 512 by 512, through lab_window) with two grey-backed rings on two pixels. Right: two swatches in the pixels' real colours: 'flat' (127, 127, 254) with an arrow pointing straight up, and 'leans' (124, 133, 254) with a slightly tilted arrow; a legend with three arrow shapes in the channel colours: 'left or right' (red), 'up or down' (green), 'upright' (blue); a number '13°' for the steepest pixel.
B26.motion_claim: The two arrows draw from the swatches (one upright, one tilted) as the voice says flat and leans; the legend arrows draw with red, green, blue.
B26.why: Colour-to-direction is a coding scheme; swatches next to arrows decode it, and the real texture proves the numbers.

B27.visual_intent: Two real 2 by 2 tilings of the normal map side by side (captures/tiles-not-seamless.png labelled 'Seamless off', captures/tiles-seamless.png labelled 'Seamless on'), each with the tile-crossing lines marked by two thin grey lines; a ring on the visible jump in the left one. Under them the measured edge jump: '53 times a normal step' for off and 'about 1 time' for on; at the top the two switch names 'As Normal Map' and 'Seamless' as outlined chips.
B27.motion_claim: The two chips light; the ring appears on the left tiling's seam; the numbers land under each picture.

show.event: chips As Normal Map and Seamless

B27.why: The seam is a picture of an edge mismatch; two real tilings next to each other show it without a word of explanation.

props.code:
group_uniforms Ripples;
uniform sampler2D normal_a : hint_normal, filter_linear_mipmap, repeat_enable;

cues.label: hint_normal: the image holds directions, not colors
repeat_enable: the address may wrap past 1

props.caption: repeat_disable smears the edge pixels; repeat_enable wraps the picture

B28.capture_spec: C19: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04e-no-repeat (repeat_disable) swapped at 55 % of the beat for 04b-scrolling-normals (repeat_enable), iso camera.
B28.visual_intent: Code card (the group and the sampler line lit twice); the real cove: first long smeared streaks of glare across most of the water, then at 55 % the streaks resolve into fine ripples.
B28.motion_claim: Long smeared streaks turn into fine ripples the instant repeat is enabled.
B28.runner_up: manim: a tile with clamped edges
B28.why: The smear is a visible bug; the real before and after proves what the hint does.

cues.label: TIME: seconds on one clock shared by the whole game

props.caption: ripple_speed: how far the address moves each second

B29.capture_spec: C20: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04b-scrolling-normals, iso camera, TIME runs from the capture start.
B29.visual_intent: Code card (the 04b fragment, the scrolled address line lit); the real cove: the glints drift steadily across the water in one direction.
B29.motion_claim: The whole glitter pattern drifts one way across the water.
B29.runner_up: manim: a window sliding over a tile
B29.why: The drifting glints are the result; a sliding window drawing would show the mechanism.

cues.label: the second layer: scaled 0.7, moving the other way
mix: blends from a to b; t of 0 gives a, 1 gives b

props.caption: two normal maps, averaged: the repeat disappears

B30.capture_spec: C21: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04b-scrolling-normals swapped at 50 % of the beat for 04c-two-layers, iso camera.
B30.visual_intent: Code card (the 04c fragment; the two address lines then the mix line lit); the real cove: one steadily drifting glint pattern, then after the swap the glints cross and shimmer with no single direction.
B30.motion_claim: A steady drift turns into crossing shimmer when the second layer arrives.
B30.why: The change from drift to shimmer is the claim and a real swap shows it; the drawing of two windows cannot.

props.caption: the near edge is the same pixel row in every column (row 487 of 720)

B31.capture_spec: C22: scene water_scene.gd, W_BARE low camera (1.1 m above the water, fov 30), shader 04d-warped-foam, plane NOT cut; the near edge was measured at row 487 of a 1280 x 720 frame in every column (evidence/planning-checks).
B31.visual_intent: The framed window shows a flat plane seen from just above the waterline: the glints and the foam net move across it, and the near and far edges stay ruler straight; a pill 'same row' sits on the near edge.
B31.motion_claim: Everything on the plane moves; its edge never does.

show.event: glints moving on a flat plane
pill same row on the near edge

B31.runner_up: manim: a straight line over a bumpy normal
B31.why: A real photograph-like render with a straight edge, measured to the pixel row, is the claim itself.

cues.label: warp: the foam's address, pushed along the lean

props.caption: warp_strength 0 to 0.4: the foam net bends with the ripples

B32.capture_spec: C23: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04d-warped-foam, warp_strength swept 0 to 0.4 across the beat, iso camera.
B32.visual_intent: Code card (the warp lines lit); the real cove: a straight-edged foam net that bends and sloshes with the ripples as the warp rises.
B32.motion_claim: The foam lines bend and slosh as the warp rises.
B32.runner_up: manim: a grid bent by arrows
B32.why: The foam net bending on the real water is the result.

props.caption: median red of the water, same shader, same clock: 132 against 100

B33.capture_spec: C24: scene water_scene.gd, shader 04d-warped-foam, iso camera, recorded twice (Forward+ and Compatibility) at 1080 x 1080 and joined side by side. The medians (132, 163, 204 against 100, 158, 205) are E15, measured on a top view of the bare plane at the same clock (evidence/planning-checks/logs/e15-renderers-ripples.txt).
B33.visual_intent: Wide window: two identical scenes side by side, both moving on the same clock: left Forward+ (a lighter, greyer blue), right Compatibility (a deeper, more saturated blue); pills 'red 132' and 'red 100'.
B33.motion_claim: Both scenes ripple in step; the right one is a deeper blue.

show.event: the warmer glints on the right

B33.why: The side by side is the claim; no drawing is as convincing as the two real renders.
